examples.knowledge_point: Dividing a Real Number by a Complex Number

feedback.worked_solution:
The denominator is $1+\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $1-\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $1-\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{3\text{i}}{1+\text{i}} & =\frac{3\text{i}}{1+\text{i}}\cdot \frac{1-\text{i}}{1-\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{3\text{i}-3{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3\text{i}-3(-1)}{1-(-1)} \\  & =\frac{3\text{i}+3}{1+1} \\  & =\frac{3\text{i}+3}{2}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{3\text{i}+3}{2}=\frac{3}{2}+\frac{3}{2}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
